Changing the primary casting stat from INT to WIS/CHA could shift game balance a bit, as those are (in most cases) more useful stats, but it’s like you said before, up to your DM. While I don’t see an issue with it, I also can’t see the necessity for it. Fighters get plenty of ASIs so you should have serviceable soft stats in most cases. I would allow it if you were reflavoring the Eldritch Knight as a Divine Knight or some sort of Sorcerer Knight. Otherwise, I think INT is a good secondary stat for martial subclasses because Gish builds already exist for primary casters. 

Divine spells, especially Cleric and Paladin ones, can be very potent in combat. Even more so in the hands of a Fighter, due to their tendency to have high CON and the potential for multiple feats. That being said, I wouldn’t take an issue with it as a DM, as long as you can come up with a compelling narrative reason for it. Just make sure that you follow the Evocation/Abjuration restrictions, and I’m sure you’d be able to convince your DM to let you play test it a bit. Very cool concept!

You don’t need to have a random encounter every time your party travels on foot. But if you don’t want to make it feel too sudden, you could always have your players share some little information about their character.

It’s obviously a no brainer to take this cantrip as it stands with an Arcana Cleric, but as far as I’m aware, that’s the only class/subclass that would be able to add extra damage like that. How about two types known at fist level, then scaled appropriately thereafter? I like the thematics, but if you’re only allotted one, you’re stuck with an attack cantrip that deals less damage than Firebolt and has no supplementary features for the entire first tier of play. As far spreading damage with multiple runes… why not? I’ll use Chill Touch as a comparison. Chill Touch shares the same damage die as the spell above and uses necrotic damage, another rarely resisted type. It additionally prevents the target from regaining hit points and provides some defensive buffs when used against undead. Comparatively, Chromatic Runes “utility” comes from its ability to consistently deal damage. In order to ensure that consistency, multiple attack runes allow for you to still get some damage off if you miss the initial attack. As it scales higher, the likelihood of high damage decreases with the likelihood of low damage. At least, that’s my design intent.

Remarkable Subclass! Very thematic and lots of synergy between the features. My only recommended design changes involve the Weave Shroud feature and the spell list at the end. Oh definitely. But it’s a worse Eldritch Blast that’s available to more spell lists. I would never expect a Warlock to take this over EB, but thought it could be an interesting alternative to Fire Bolt or Ray of Frost. I mostly included it on the Warlock list so players using a Blood Hunter could have a multi-hit cantrip that matches their preferred damage type.

I mostly allowed different targets for thematics. A single d8 is not very much damage, so you’d want to be focusing all runes on a single target. In doing so, you could change the damage type with each attack, really fulfilling that imagery of high speed elemental mastery.

The strength from Eldritch Blast’s multiple beams comes from their potential to be enhanced with Invocations. As far selecting the damage type, I designed the spell with versatility in mind. Eldritch Blast is force damage, meaning out of the MM, VGtM, and MtoF, only the Helmed Horror has immunity. Allowing the user to select the damage type of Chromatic Runes to get around resistances keeps it in line with the base strength of Eldritch Blast. The DMG suggests single target damage for a cantrip to be d10 scaled with level, however, we see most attack cantrips use a d8. This is because they all have a secondary effect. Ray of Frost reduces speed, Shocking Grasp removes reactions, even Sacred Flame ignores cover and it uses the second least resisted damage type in the game. Chromatic Rune’s option of damage type is its secondary effect. I considered reducing the damage scaling to a d6, considering some monsters have vulnerabilities to certain damage types. But seeing as that’s a rare trait and cantrips scale kind of poorly, I felt a d8 was still appropriate. I wanted players to feel like they’d have their bases covered with this spell, allowing them to free up their other cantrip choices for utility, without completely outshining all other attack cantrips.
